children: Meritage Hospitality Group
, one of Wendy’s
largest U.S. franchisees, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection as the restaurant operator seeks to restructure its finances amid weak sales at the burger chain.
The Grand Rapids, Michigan-based company operates 314 Wendy’s
restaurants across the Midwest and Southeast, as well as one Bojangles location and five Morning Belle restaurants, according to Nation’s Restaurant News.
Meritage
listed between $10 million and $50 million in assets and liabilities in its bankruptcy filing and has about $150 million in debt owed to City National Bank, NRN reported.
The filing follows Meritage’s
closure of 60 Wendy’s

restaurants earlier this year as the company moved to reduce costs and improve profitability. It has also stopped or modified breakfast service at underperforming locations, according to the publication.
Meritage

said the bankruptcy process would help strengthen its balance sheet and provide greater financial flexibility. The company also plans to seek debtor-in-possession financing to support operations while it restructures.
Wendy’s
has struggled with declining sales and traffic in the U.S. Same-store sales fell 7% in the second quarter, prompting the company to cut its dividend and withdraw its financial outlook for the year.
Wendy’s
said it works with franchisees facing financial challenges on a case-by-case basis and remains focused on supporting its franchise system.
Meritage
said it remains confident in the potential for a turnaround of the Wendy’s
brand.
Shares of Wendy
were trading about 4% lower in the afternoon trade on Friday.
